html:
Lagos Colony was the British colony around the island port of Lagos in what is now south-western Nigeria, from 1861 to 1906. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900.

Lagos had been a busy port of the Atlantic slave trade. After Britain banned the trade, a British naval attack in 1851 drove out King Kosoko and put his rival on the throne. In 1861 King Dosunmu was pressed to cede the town, and it became a colony.

Lagos grew fast as a trading town for palm oil. Freed slaves returning from Sierra Leone and from Brazil settled there and formed an educated, Christian elite of clerks, traders and clergy. From Lagos the British extended their influence over the Yoruba wars inland and over Ibadan. In 1906 the colony merged into Southern Nigeria, and in 1914 Lagos became the capital of all Nigeria.
